facts.statement: Caiuajara was an extinct genus of tapejarid pterosaur that lived in Brazil during the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Caiuajara is an extinct genus of tapejarid pterosaur from the Early Cretaceous period (Aptian to Albian stages) of Brazil.

facts.statement: The genus Caiuajara is known from a single species, Caiuajara dobruskii.
facts.quote: It is known from a single type species, Caiuajara dobruskii.

facts.statement: Pterosaur fossils were discovered in 1971 by laborers Alexandre Dobruski and his son João Gustavo Dobruski near Cruzeiro do Oeste in the state of Paraná, Brazil.
facts.quote: In 1971, the labourers Alexandre Dobruski and his son João Gustavo Dobruski found pterosaur fossils in a field near Cruzeiro do Oeste in the south of Brazil, in the state of Paraná.

facts.statement: The species Caiuajara dobruskii was formally named and described in 2014 by a team including Paulo Manzig and Alexander Kellner.
facts.quote: In 2014, the type species Caiuajara dobruskii was named and described by Paulo Manzig, Alexander Kellner, Luiz Weinschütz, Carlos Fragoso, Cristina Vega, Gilson Guimarães, Luiz Godoy, Antonio Liccardo, João Ricetti and Camila de Moura.

facts.statement: The generic name Caiuajara honors the geological Caiuá Group and is related to the genus Tapejara.
facts.quote: The generic name refers to the geological Caiuá Group and the related genus Tapejara.

facts.statement: The specific name dobruskii honors the fossil discoverers, Alexandre and João Gustavo Dobruski.
facts.quote: The specific name honors the discoverers.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was found in the Goio-Erê Formation within the Paraná Basin.
facts.quote: The holotype, CP.V 1449, was found in a sandstone layer of the Goio-Erê Formation, of Early Cretaceous age, in the Paraná Basin.

facts.statement: Hundreds of bones representing at least forty-seven individuals have been discovered in bone beds.
facts.quote: Many hundreds of bones have been discovered, concentrated in several bone beds, and representing at least forty-seven individuals but probably many more.

facts.statement: Most discovered individuals are juveniles, while adults are rare and represented by only two skulls and three humeri.
facts.quote: The individuals found are often juveniles; adult animals are much rarer, only represented by two skulls and three humeri.

facts.statement: Adult Caiuajara possessed a large toothless head with an enormous shark-fin-shaped crest on the snout.
facts.quote: The species had a large toothless head with, in adult individuals, an enormous shark fin-shaped crest on the snout.

facts.statement: The tip of the snout is oriented downward at an angle of 142 to 149 degrees relative to the upper jaw edge.
facts.quote: The tip of the snout is strongly oriented to below, at 142 to 149°, relative to the edge of the upper jaw.

facts.statement: The pteroid bone features a conspicuous depression on its bottom surface that lacks a pneumatic opening.
facts.quote: The pteroid on its bottom surface shows a conspicuous depression lacking a pneumatic opening.

facts.statement: Caiuajara is classified within the family Tapejaridae, specifically the subfamily Tapejarinae.
facts.quote: Caiuajara was assigned to the Tapejaridae, more precisely the Tapejarinae.

facts.statement: A 2019 phylogenetic analysis placed Caiuajara within the tribe Tapejarini as a sister taxon to a group containing Europejara, Tapejara, and Tupandactylus.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis conducted in 2019 by Kellner (one of the describers of Caiuajara) and colleagues recovered Caiuajara within the tribe Tapejarini, sister taxon to sister taxon to three other genera: Europejara, Tapejara, and Tupandactylus.

facts.statement: In 2014, Caiuajara was considered the geologically youngest known tapejarid and the most southern one known.
facts.quote: In 2014, Caiuajara was the geologically youngest known tapejarid (aside from the possible tapejarid Bakonydraco galaczi) and also the most southern one known.

facts.statement: Caiuajara represents the first pterosaur fossil discovered in southern Brazil.
facts.quote: Moreover, Caiuajara is the first pterosaur found in the south of Brazil.

facts.statement: Caiuajara lived in a desert environment featuring dunes.
facts.quote: The habitat of Caiuajara was a desert with dunes.

facts.statement: Large fossil concentrations suggest Caiuajara lived in colonies, indicating a gregarious lifestyle.
facts.quote: The large concentrations of fossils, which are rare among pterosaurs and only equaled by those found of the Argentine form Pterodaustro, were interpreted as evidence of a gregarious lifestyle, with Caiuajara living in colonies.

facts.statement: The predominance of juvenile fossils suggests possible creching behavior where young formed groups separate from adults.
facts.quote: The majority of Caiuajara specimens are juveniles, and it is possible that this reflects creching behavior, where young individuals formed large groups separately from most of the adult individuals.

facts.statement: The accumulation of juveniles and subadults may indicate a nursery site near an inland lake.
facts.quote: The accumulation of juvenile and subadult Caiuajara individuals may represent a nursery near an inland lake.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests Caiuajara were precocial, capable of flight shortly after hatching, implying limited parental care.
facts.quote: This suggests that they were precocial, taking wing almost as soon as they hatched; parental care must have been limited.

facts.statement: The snout crest grew significantly taller and steeper during development, changing inclination from about 115 degrees to 90 degrees.
facts.quote: The snout crest however, strongly changed during growth. It became much taller and also much more steeply inclined, from about 115° to 90°.

facts.statement: The absence of crestless specimens indicates Caiuajara was not sexually dimorphic regarding the crest, challenging the hypothesis that pterosaurs were normally sexually dimorphic.
facts.quote: No specimens have been found lacking the snout crest, indicating that Caiuajara was in this respect not sexually dimorphic and casting doubt on the hypothesis that pterosaurs normally were.

facts.statement: Histological analysis shows Caiuajara had a rapid growth rate with higher bone deposition rates than Rhamphorhynchus and Pterodaustro.
facts.quote: Analysis of histological sections of Caiuajara bones demonstrate that it had a rapid growth rate, with higher rates of bone deposition than in Rhamphorhynchus and Pterodaustro.

facts.statement: Caiuajara maintained a high metabolism throughout its life, unlike Rhamphorhynchus and Pterodaustro which developed lower metabolisms with age.
facts.quote: Notably, Caiuajara retains a high metabolism through its life, whereas Rhamphorhynchus and Pterodaustro developed lower metabolisms with age.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Caiuajara was herbivorous, as no fossil plants have been found associated with the fossils despite tapejarids often being assumed to be herbivores.
facts.quote: Fossil plants — tapejarids are often assumed to have been herbivores — have not been found, so there are no direct indications about the food source.

facts.statement: It is debated whether mass mortality was caused by storms or droughts.
facts.quote: Possibly the same storms caused many individuals to die together; this could also have been the result of droughts.

facts.statement: The genus Caiuajara was named and described by Manzig et al. in 2014.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Manzig et al., 2014

facts.statement: Caiuajara lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Cretácico Superior

facts.statement: Caiuajara is an extinct genus of tapejarid pterosaur that lived in what is now Brazil.
facts.quote: Caiuajara es un género extinto de pterosaurio tapejárido que vivió durante el Cretácico Superior en lo que ahora es Brasil.

facts.statement: Fossils of pterosaurs were found in 1971 by workers Alexandre Dobruski and his son João Gustavo Dobruski near Cruzeiro do Oeste in Paraná, southern Brazil.
facts.quote: En 1971, los jornaleros Alexandre Dobruski y su hijo João Gustavo Dobruski encontraron fósiles de pterosaurios en un campo cercano a Cruzeiro do Oeste en el sur de Brasil, en el estado de Paraná.

facts.statement: The genus name refers to the Caiuá geological formation and the related genus Tapejara.
facts.quote: El nombre del género se refiere a la unidad geológica Grupo Caiuá y al género relacionado Tapejara.

facts.statement: The species name "dobruskii" honors its discoverers.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie, "dobruskii", es en homenaje de sus descubridores.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen dates to approximately 87 million years ago, likely from the Coniacian-Campanian stages.
facts.quote: El holotipo, CP.V 1449, fue hallado en una capa de arenisca de la Formación Goio-Erê, cuya edad es incierta; quizás data del Coniaciense-Campaniense, hace aproximadamente 87 millones de años.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial skeleton including the skull, jaw, neck vertebrae, and wing elements.
facts.quote: Consiste de un esqueleto parcial que incluye el cráneo, la mandíbula, vértebras del cuello y elementos de las alas.

facts.statement: Most found individuals were young, while adult specimens are rare.
facts.quote: La mayoría de los individuos encontrados son jóvenes, los animales adultos son escasos.

facts.statement: The largest individuals of Caiuajara had an estimated wingspan of 2.35 meters.
facts.quote: Los mayores individuos de Caiuajara tenían una envergadura estimada en 2.35 metros.

facts.statement: This species had a large toothless head and adults possessed an enormous crest resembling a shark fin over their snout.
facts.quote: Esta especie tenía una gran cabeza sin dientes y en los individuos adultos, una enorme cresta algo parecida a la aleta de un tiburón sobre su hocico.

facts.statement: The snout tip pointed downward at angles of 142 to 149 degrees relative to the upper jaw edge.
facts.quote: La punta del hocico se orienta notablemente hacia abajo, en ángulos de 142 a 149°, en relación con el borde de la mandíbula superior.

facts.statement: Caiuajara lived in a desert habitat with dunes.
facts.quote: El hábitat de Caiuajara era un desierto con dunas.

facts.statement: No fossil plants have been found, so there are no direct indicators of its food source, though tapejarids are generally believed to be herbivores.
facts.quote: Plantas fósiles — se cree generalmente que los tapejáridos eran herbívoros — no han sido encontradas, por lo que no hay indicadores directos de su fuente de alimentos.

facts.statement: Large fossil concentrations, comparable only to the Argentine genus Pterodaustro, are considered evidence of a gregarious lifestyle.
facts.quote: Las grandes concentraciones de fósiles, solo igualadas por el género argentino Pterodaustro, son considerados por los autores como prueba de un estilo de vida gregario.

facts.statement: No crestless specimens have been found, indicating Caiuajara was not sexually dimorphic regarding the crest and challenging the hypothesis that pterosaurs normally exhibited such dimorphism.
facts.quote: No se han hallado especímenes que carezcan de la cresta, lo que indica que Caiuajara en este aspecto no era sexualmente dimórfico y cuestiona la hipótesis de que los pterosaurios normalmente presentaban dicho dimorfismo.

facts.statement: The fossil record for Caiuajara spans from the Aptian to the Campanian stages, between 121.4 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Campanian (121.4 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: A study by Araújo et al. (2026) suggests Caiuajara dobruskii had metabolic rates intermediate between modern ectotherms and endotherms and was likely capable of prolonged powered flight.
facts.quote: Araújo et al. (2026) use the data from the study of bone histology of Caiuajara dobruskii to calculate its resting and maximum metabolic rates, recovered as intermediate between those of modern ectothermic and endothermic amniotes, and interpret C. dobruskii as likely capable of prolonged powered flight.
